question: How are the principles of desire and poison understood in their true nature?
premises: The principle of desire is fullness, clearly perceived in the collision of energies.
The principle of poison is nectar.
Poison becomes nectar when the covering of the limited self has fallen away.
inference: Desire and poison reveal their highest nature as fullness and nectar when experienced without the contraction of the limited self.
uncertainties: The exact referent of 'saṃghaṭṭa' (collision) may be sexual, energetic, or cognitive depending on context.
plain_english: The true nature of desire is fullness, clearly seen in the moment of collision; and the true nature of poison is nectar, once the covering of the limited self has dropped away.
